objectives: Use Lesson 29 evidence to select a specific /n/ remediation target.
Correct initial /n/, final /n/, spelling, fluency or comprehension weaknesses.
Reassess the same target and make an evidence-based advance-or-reteach decision.
concepts: Remediation should match the diagnosed error.
Initial and final phoneme confusions require different practice.
Fluency intervention should preserve accuracy and meaning.
Reassessment determines whether another cycle is necessary.

definitions.definition: Focused instruction designed to correct one identified learning weakness.
A follow-up measure of the same skill after targeted instruction.
A documented decision to progress or provide another targeted practice cycle based on reassessment evidence.

workedExamples: nap/map → isolate initial /n/ and /m/, practise contrast, then reread.
man/mat → isolate final /n/ and /t/, practise contrast, then spell and read.
Slow accurate passage reading → repeated controlled rereading with meaning checks.
commonMistakes: Using one generic remediation for every learner.
Treating speed as the only fluency measure.
Testing a different skill instead of the diagnosed target.
revisionPoints: Diagnose → target → model → practise → reassess → advance/reteach.

conceptual: Match common errors to appropriate remediation.
application: Apply correction strategies to n-containing CVC words.
higherOrderThinking: Choose whether evidence supports advancement or reteaching.
mixedReview: Decode, spell, reread and comprehend after targeted practice.

formulaOrFactBank: Remediation decision = target evidence + reassessment evidence
weakTopicRevision: Repeat only the diagnosed pathway and reassess before advancing.

outcomes: Learner corrects a targeted initial or final /n/ error with at least 80% accuracy.
Learner spells targeted n-containing CVC words with at least 80% accuracy.
Learner improves smoothness without sacrificing decoding accuracy.
Learner answers targeted controlled-text questions with at least 80% accuracy.
Learner receives an explicit evidence-based advance-or-reteach decision.

questions.question: A learner reads “nap” as “map.” Which sound needs targeted practice?
A learner reads “man” as “mat.” Which sound needs targeted practice?
A learner spells “nap” as “map.” What should be corrected?
A learner spells “man” as “mat.” What should be corrected?
A learner reads accurately but very slowly. Which practice is most appropriate?
options: Repeated accurate reading of controlled text

questions.question: A learner answers a passage question incorrectly but decoded every word. What should be practised?
options: Rereading for meaning and locating text evidence

questions.question: What should happen after targeted modelling?
options: Guided practice followed by an independent attempt
Immediate introduction of a new phoneme

questions.question: Why should reassessment use the same skill target?
options: To determine whether the diagnosed weakness improved

questions.question: A learner improves on initial /n/ after targeted practice. What should happen next?
options: Record improvement and continue to the next needed skill

questions.question: A learner still misses final /n/. What is the appropriate response?
options: Provide another final-/n/ practice cycle before advancing

questions.question: Which activity best targets /n/ versus /m/?
options: Compare nap/map and say the first sound

questions.question: Which activity best targets final /n/ versus /t/?
options: Compare man/mat and isolate the final sound

questions.question: Which evidence supports improved n decoding?
options: Accurate independent reading across several taught n words

questions.question: Which evidence supports improved comprehension?
options: Correct answers supported by the controlled text

questions.question: What is the purpose of this lesson?
options: Correct diagnosed /n/ weaknesses and verify improvement before advancing
